#6237. 17 Trips You Should Book a Year in Advance

I'm a firm believer that holidays need a balance of organization and freedom, so that you can enjoy all the long-awaited activities without feeling like they're obligations. Starting to organize and book excursions well in advance can make your experience considerably better, especially when planning trips to particularly popular destinations. Though, that's not the only reason why you should already be thinking about what to add to your 2027 travel bucket list.

Planning a trip a year in advance, long before your suitcase ever leaves the closet, offers up a very particular and potent type of dopamine hit. The moment you confirm a flight or secure a coveted reservation delivers its own quiet thrill, a reminder that the joy of travel lives not only in the trip itself, but in the anticipation that precedes it.

With 2027 shaping up to be a year of more personal, experience-led travel, there's even more reason to start planning ahead. According to Booking.com's 2027 travel predictions, 77 percent of travelers are interested in taking a holiday that pushes them beyond their comfort zone, while 81 percent would choose a destination based on how they want to feel rather than simply where they want to go.

Booking early has myriad practical advantages, too. It can protect you from soaring prices, guarantee access to peak-season experiences, and ensure a plethora of accommodation options that often fill up months before departure. The extra planning room also allows you to seek out lesser-known routes and time your visit to seasonal spectacles. Plus, it offers the underrated delight of months filled with small frissons of excitement every time you think about what is to come. Whether you’re dreaming of spotting wildlife in East Africa or weaving through the Peloponnese in Greece, here's your guide to planning a trip a year in advance for 2027.

This gallery has been updated since its original publish date.

England’s landscapes offer a surprising breadth of adventure for such a compact country, from the rugged drama of the Lake District to the chalk cliffs and wildflower-strewn downs of the South East and the mellow, biscuit-hued villages that string all of this together. A rich tapestry of moors that feel wonderfully remote, market towns that hum with independent food producers, and stretches of coastline where seals bob with the rhythm of the waves can all be woven together, with the added ease of just being able to ring up and book. Outdoorsy types can opt for hiking along windswept coastal paths in Cornwall, paddleboarding through still-water estuaries in Devon, or following ancient woodland trails in the New Forest, while those who prefer a slower pace can settle into long lunches at quaint English vineyards (Chapel Down in Kent and Rathfinny in Sussex, to name a few), wander through sculpture parks or spend languid afternoons in honey-stone villages where the loudest sound is often the church bell.

For those seeking the same sense of escape on a gentler scale, a clutch of estates across England is quietly rethinking the country house stay. Just outside London, The Grove in Hertfordshire is a firm family favorite, amid rolling parkland and its own championship golf course. The addition of two quaint cottages tucked into the grounds in 2025 offers a more private way to experience the estate, with access to its extensive grounds and family-friendly activities, from mini Land Rover rides to archery and woodland walks. Further north, The Tawny in Staffordshire offers a more immersive relationship with the landscape, where architecturally considered treehouses and lakeside retreats complement woodland gardens, dining at The Plumicorn restaurant, and paths to explore across its two adjoining estates. While in Hampshire, Avington Park Estate leans into its historic setting, pairing grand riverside scenery with elegant accommodation and access to fishing, wild swimming, and a range of wellness experiences, including a lakeside sauna pod.

All this, though, with the caveat that some of the most sought-after Great British stays can fill up well ahead of peak weekends and school holidays, so it's worth getting your reservation in early if you have your heart set on a particular property or date in 2027.

The Peloponnese invites a slower, deeper kind of Greek escape, one built around winding coastal roads, mountain passes scented with wild herbs, and ancient sites that appear almost without warning. This southern peninsula feels far removed from the island throngs, yet it offers a richness that rivals any Aegean hotspot. Planning ahead is key, particularly if you want to secure small guesthouses, family-run inns, or farm stays in popular coastal areas during July and August. For a 2027 trip, consider traveling in May, June, or September, when temperatures are generally more comfortable for sightseeing and the roads are less crowded than at the height of summer.

A favorite among avid road trippers, routes here weave through layers of history and landscape. One moment you’re exploring the fortified town of Monemvasia, built on a towering rocky islet connected to the mainland by a narrow causeway, and the next you are wandering through the ruins of Mycenae or the venerable theater at Epidaurus. The distances are manageable with a well-planned itinerary, which leaves ample time to pause at quiet coves, watch fishermen haul in their morning catch, or break for lunch under vine-covered pergolas in medieval villages. Allow at least a week if you want to explore several parts of the peninsula rather than rushing between archaeological sites, and consider choosing a handful of bases, such as Nafplio, Monemvasia, the Mani peninsula, or Pylos, to make the most of the journey.

The Mani peninsula is stark and dramatic, dotted with stone towers and rugged beaches that glow at sunset. To the west, the region opens into long ribbons of sand, olive groves that stretch toward the horizon, and wetlands alive with birdlife. Near Pylos, the Gialova Lagoon is an important stopping point for migratory birds, while the nearby crescent-shaped Voidokilia Beach makes a particularly tempting stop on a coastal drive. Inland, the mountains of Arcadia offer cool respite in summer and timeless hiking trails that trace the contours of rivers and valleys. If you're traveling in 2027, book your preferred accommodation early for peak summer dates, but leave enough room in the itinerary for spontaneous detours. In fact, for travelers drawn to the romance of the open road, there are few places as rewarding or as effortlessly cinematic as the Peloponnese.

For couples planning a celebration trip, Hawaii remains one of the most evocative places to unwind together. The archipelago pairs volcanic drama with serene beaches, vibrant reefs, and an open spirit, while its deeply held sense of community gives romance a grounded, almost effortless quality.

For a romantic escape, the choice of island is just as important as the hotel. On Big Island, volcanic landscapes and stretches of coastline set the scene for a slower-paced holiday, while Oahu combines beautiful beaches with Honolulu's lively restaurants and nightlife. The hotel scene offers plenty of tempting options, from the traditional-style, thatched-roof hale at Rosewood Kona Village and the extensively renovated Mauna Lani, Auberge Collection, to smaller gems such as White Sands Hotel and Surfjack in Waikiki.

For a honeymoon or anniversary trip, it's worth booking your preferred resort and flights in advance, particularly if you're traveling over Christmas, New Year, or during the summer holidays. And if you're hoping to explore more than one island, allow enough time for the additional flights rather than trying to squeeze too much into one trip.

The landscapes of Utah are full of sandstone spires, rust-red cliffs that glow in the late-afternoon light, and labyrinthine slot canyons that twist into shadow and sun. Geology becomes a storybook, particularly at Utahraptor State Park, home to one of the most significant dinosaur bone sites in North America. Located around 15 miles northwest of Moab, the park protects the Dalton Wells Dinosaur Quarry, where thousands of dinosaur bones have been discovered, including those of its namesake predator. Further south, the astonishing petroglyph panels at Newspaper Rock offer a rare glimpse into centuries of Indigenous history, with carvings attributed to Basketmaker, Ancestral Puebloan, and Ute peoples. The rock surface is carved with scenes that feel as vivid today as when they were first etched.

Both sites can be reached from Moab, a small desert hub that continues to evolve. From April to early November 2027, Canyon Spirit, formerly Rocky Mountaineer's Rockies to the Red Rocks service, is scheduled to operate its two-day train journey between Denver and Moab, with an overnight stay in Glenwood Springs. With panoramic windows framing Colorado's mountains, river valleys, and dramatic red-rock canyons, it is a journey that turns the simple act of moving from one place to another into an experience in its own right. Winter, too, brings a different kind of spectacle to Utah, when canyon walls catch the low light and snowfall softens the edges of its famously rugged terrain. For a 2027 trip, it's worth securing your preferred train departure and accommodation in Moab well ahead, particularly if you're traveling in spring or autumn, when temperatures are generally more comfortable for exploring the desert on foot.

Vancouver Island offers a rare kind of quiet that settles over old-growth forests, wild shorelines, and mountain lakes so still they resemble polished stone. It is also a place where Indigenous presence remains central. The lands of the Kwakwaka’wakw, Nuu-chah-nulth, and Coast Salish peoples continue to shape the island’s identity, and planning ahead allows travelers to seek out experiences rooted in cultural respect rather than commercial interpretation. Ferries can fill up quickly during summer, making advance bookings worthwhile on reservable routes and giving you time to curate a thoughtful route. BC Ferries generally opens reservations six months ahead and recommends booking at least four to six weeks before long weekends, so it's worth planning your crossings early if you're traveling with a car or camper van.

On the water, you can join marine excursions informed by generations of coastal knowledge or explore the Salish Sea with Indigenous guides who share their knowledge of the region's history, wildlife, and cultural traditions. Fishing trips with Indigenous-owned outfitters offer another way to experience the island's coastal traditions, while storytelling walks and wildlife encounters reveal how land, sea, and culture are intertwined. Vancouver Island’s landscapes match this richness. Orcas pulse through cold channels, black bears forage along shorelines and in forest clearings, and mist drifts between cedar trees that have stood for centuries. Whether you pitch a tent north of Campbell River or take a slow-rolling road trip in a camper van, this is a destination where the outside world becomes the centerpiece. Summer is a particularly rewarding time to explore, with longer days for hiking and kayaking, while whale-watching opportunities vary by location and season. If you're planning a 2027 escape, check campsite reservation opening dates and arrange popular guided wildlife excursions and Indigenous-led experiences ahead of your visit, particularly for July and August.

Your kids might learn about the rainforest at school—but there’s nothing like seeing it in real life to nurture their interest in nature and inspire their curiosity. Costa Rica is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world, with more than a quarter of its territory protected for conservation, and it’s not just children who are enchanted by bright butterflies, noisy green macaws, bead-eyed tree frogs, and sloths. It’s a relatively small country, so it’s possible to take in the rainforest canopy, pineapple plantations, sandy beaches, and mist-topped mountains all in one trip. From spotting wildlife on guided rainforest walks to exploring hanging bridges around Arenal or watching the waves roll in along the Pacific coast, there are plenty of ways to turn a family holiday into an adventure.

The best eco-lodges, home rentals, and hotels in Costa Rica are worth booking well ahead, particularly for Christmas, Easter, and school holidays. The Pacific coast's dry season generally runs from December to March, with April marking the transition towards the rainy season, making these months popular for beach holidays and outdoor adventures. The Caribbean coast follows a different rainfall pattern, with September and October often among its driest months. Plan in advance and book into one of the country's famous eco-friendly stays—we like the Victorian-style bungalows at Aguas Claras in Puerto Viejo or the luxurious Lapa Rios Lodge on the Osa Peninsula. Aguas Claras welcomes children aged three and over and can arrange activities such as surfing lessons and wildlife excursions, while Lapa Rios, which accepts children aged six and over, offers guided rainforest experiences and opportunities to learn about conservation. For a private stay, there are some truly fantastic Airbnbs in Costa Rica, including treehouses surrounded by tropical greenery and villas near the beaches of Santa Teresa.

For a 2027 family trip, it's worth planning your route as carefully as your accommodation. Winding mountain roads and travel times between regions can make an ambitious itinerary tiring, particularly with younger children. Choose a few bases rather than trying to see everything, and book popular guided activities ahead of time. Some national parks also require advance online tickets, so check the relevant booking arrangements before visiting.

Though Seoul is famous for its café culture and culinary scene, the kitchens in South Korea's southern regions are drawing travelers down and out of the capital, with tour operators designing itineraries that guide guests through the ingredients, culture, and history of each recipe. Responsible Travel has put together an eight-day experience with departures available throughout much of 2027, inviting travelers to experience regional specialities, spend a night at a Buddhist temple near Gyeongju, explore traditional food markets, and learn to make kimchi. On the coast, Jeollanam-do spotlights fresher, lighter flavors straight from the ocean such as ganjang gejang (soy-marinated crab), plus richer dishes like beef-rib soup. You can also stay in a temple at Baekyangsa, where Buddhist nun and chef Jeong Kwan (of Chef’s Table fame) has a meditative approach to Korean cooking. The temple offers a separate overnight experience featuring a demonstration of her temple cuisine, with sessions generally held monthly and dates released around a month in advance.

Most arriving by air will travel through Seoul at some point—so factor in a few days to check out chefs such as Jungsik Yim and Mingoo Kang, who have been putting the city on the Michelin-starred map with their internationally-acclaimed menus. Kang's restaurant Mingles holds three Michelin stars in the 2026 guide, while Yim's Jungsik has two, making both tempting additions to a food-focused itinerary. For an authentic stay, book into a hanok in Seoul, perhaps in the historic Bukchon neighborhood, where traditional tiled-roof houses sit alongside galleries, tea rooms, and small boutiques. Be aware that tourist sightseeing is restricted between 5 p.m. and 10 a.m. in designated residential streets, so check the local rules before visiting.

Ask most people what’s on their travel bucket list, and you can guarantee that a trip on Belmond's Venice Simplon-Orient-Express is up there. Long associated with romance and timeless glamour, there are few things as enjoyable as a journey on one of these famous trains through Europe. Thanks to a focus on slow travel, you can now justify your ticket as a greener way of getting around. From the moment you arrive at the station and the lacquered dark blue carriages come into view, you feel like you’ve stepped into the pages of an Agatha Christie novel.

There are 70 routes to explore, including Paris to Verona and Amsterdam to Venice. On the Florence to Paris route, squeeze in a stay at Castello di Casole beforehand so you can start your trip with freshly cooked pizza from the hotel’s 16th-century pizza oven and glasses of wine from their vineyard while watching the sun set behind the rolling Tuscan hills.

Once on board and directed to your cabin, there’s little to do but sit back, sip Champagne, and watch as the train station melts away and towns and fields speed past you. A three-course lunch in one of the three 1920s dining cars is next, followed by an afternoon drinking cocktails in 3674, the train’s Art Deco bar car, before dressing in your finery for the evening.

Time slips away as quickly as the snow-capped mountains whizzing past the window, and after a decadent dinner followed by martinis in the bar car—accompanied by the tinkling of a piano and, if you’re lucky, a sing-song from the bar staff—it’s time to climb into bed and let the movement of the train (and aforementioned martinis) lull you to sleep.

If you don’t quite manage the 6 a.m. wake up to see the sunrise over Champagne, then you’ll stir as the train pulls into Paris and coffee and pastries arrive promptly at your cabin. All that’s left is to wonder how quickly you can save for your next Venice Simplon-Orient-Express adventure. With 2027 journeys already available to book, it's worth reserving early if you have a particular route, date, or cabin category in mind.

Uruguay’s summer runs from December to February, although warm weather and beach holidays can extend into March, so it’s a popular winter break for sun-starved travelers (and when seasonal restaurants and hotels are most likely to be open). While Montevideo offers a mix of city beaches, markets, and culture, further along the coast, José Ignacio—a former fishing village turned bustling beach town—draws a fashionable crowd of locals and foreigners. The area has become a magnet for art lovers, foodies, and design enthusiasts, with places such as Posada Ayana, home to James Turrell’s Skyspace installation, and Luz, a wine lodge surrounded by vineyards and olive groves, around ten minutes' drive from José Ignacio. Guests at Posada Ayana can experience Turrell's Ta Khut installation at sunrise and sunset, while Luz offers wine tastings and culinary experiences that make it worth venturing away from the beach.

Seafront favorite Playa Vik continues to attract visitors with its striking architecture, art-filled interiors, and views over Playa Mansa. Just out of town, the high-design Sacromonte Landscape Hotel offers a more secluded escape in the wild sierras of Maldonado, where contemporary cabins overlook the surrounding vineyards and countryside. Although Francis Mallmann’s restaurants Chiringuito and Bodega Garzón are on many bucket lists, few know that visitors can also stay at Casa Anna, the chef's charming guesthouse in nearby Pueblo Garzón. Alongside regular accommodation, Casa Anna offers separately arranged hosted culinary experiences with Mallmann, including shared meals and opportunities to discover his distinctive approach to open-fire cooking.

If you're planning to spend the last of your annual leave in the South American sunshine, aim for late December to experience José Ignacio at its buzziest, but be prepared for higher prices and limited availability at the most sought-after hotels. February and March can offer a quieter alternative, although some seasonal businesses begin winding down as summer draws to a close. For the festive period, booking in advance is particularly worthwhile, especially if you're hoping to secure one of the area's smaller, design-led retreats.

The ski-in-ski-out Park Hyatt Niseko Hanazono boasts Molière Montagne, a restaurant from three-Michelin-starred chef Hiroshi Nakamichi, an impressive selection of restaurants and bars, and hot-spring bathing facilities for unwinding after a day on the slopes. Sansui Niseko offers a fully serviced alternative to townhouses by Kasara or Airbnb (the latter of which are particularly high quality here), with direct ski access to Grand Hirafu's Family Course, an onsen, and spacious suites for those traveling with family or friends.

The outskirts of Sapporo are stunning in the fall, with koyo (the appearance of autumn leaves) at its most colorful around mid-October, but winter is when Niseko really comes into its own. The 2026 to 2027 ski season is scheduled to begin on November 28, with some ski areas planning to remain open into early May, depending on snowfall. January and February are generally the best months for the famously light, dry powder that draws skiers and snowboarders from around the world, although snow conditions can never be guaranteed.

For a trip during the winter season, booking accommodation, ski lessons, and equipment rentals well in advance is a good idea, particularly over Christmas and New Year's Eve. With four interconnected ski areas, a thriving restaurant scene, and plenty of opportunities to warm up in an onsen after a day in the snow, Niseko is the kind of destination where a little advance planning can make all the difference.

Another blockbuster backdrop, Jordan’s archaeological city of Petra was named one of the new seven wonders of the world in 2007 for its extraordinary rock-carved architecture and the Al Siq canyon. A couple of hours' drive from Petra, the sliver of Red Sea coast around Aqaba draws visitors for its sun, souks, and scuba-diving opportunities, with colorful coral reefs and warm waters making it a favorite among underwater explorers. Beyond the coast, the extraordinary landscapes of Wadi Rum are another reason to add Jordan to your 2027 travel wish list. Here, towering sandstone formations and vast desert valleys provide the setting for guided excursions with local Bedouin communities and nights spent beneath the stars at desert camps.

Spring and autumn are among the best times to visit, with milder temperatures making it easier to explore Petra's archaeological treasures and venture into the desert. If you fly into the capital, Amman, a metropolis of ancient tradition and entrepreneurial spirit greets you, alongside a slew of social enterprises such as SEP, a fashion and lifestyle brand working with Palestinian refugee embroiderers, and Beit Sitti, a cooking school founded by three sisters where visitors can learn to prepare traditional Arabic dishes alongside local women.

For those hoping to combine Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Red Sea in one trip, planning ahead allows time to arrange local guides, accommodation, and transport between the country's most spectacular destinations. It's also worth looking into the Jordan Pass, which includes admission to more than 40 attractions, including Petra, and a tourist visa fee waiver for eligible visitors who purchase it before arrival and meet the relevant stay requirements. With travel schedules and regional conditions subject to change, check the latest official advisories before confirming your 2027 plans.

Antarctic travel is still trying to strike a balance between overtourism and sustainable travel, with the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators recording more than 113,000 tourists traveling to the region during the 2025 to 2026 season. Once accessible only to wealthy explorers or well-funded scientists, it’s exciting that this stark, striking landscape is now attracting a growing number of adventurous travelers, although its increasing popularity raises important questions about protecting one of the world's most fragile environments. Many choose to visit during the austral summer (November to March), when there’s less sea ice and more sun (ideal for kayaking, wildlife watching and, on certain specialist expeditions, skiing and snowshoeing).

From vast penguin colonies and seals resting on ice floes to humpback whales feeding in the Southern Ocean, Antarctica offers extraordinary opportunities for wildlife encounters, both on land and at sea. For many travelers, a polar cruise is one of the most rewarding ways to experience the continent, with expedition vessels offering guided shore landings and Zodiac excursions, while larger ships may provide scenic cruising without disembarkation. Choosing an operator committed to responsible tourism is essential, although even carefully managed expeditions have an environmental footprint. Consider a vessel with hybrid-electric propulsion, such as Ponant’s Le Commandant Charcot, the first hybrid-electric polar exploration ship powered by liquified natural gas, which also carries two onboard scientific laboratories. Or, book with an operator such as Abercrombie & Kent or White Desert, which offers a different way to experience the continent through its fly-in expeditions and luxury land-based camps, including Whichaway Camp.

With the Antarctic travel season concentrated into just a few months and places on specialist expeditions limited, planning a year ahead is particularly worthwhile. Travelers hoping to visit during the popular summer months of December and January (or to secure a place on a small-group expedition) should start comparing itineraries and booking well before departure.

Trekking in the Himalayas comes with its own set of logistical, financial, and physical challenges, so booking well in advance can make a huge difference. Big groups will struggle with spontaneity, and allowing yourself several months to train and prepare for long days on the mountains is well worth the effort. But physical preparation is only part of the equation: Ladakh's high altitude means visitors also need to allow sufficient time to acclimate, particularly when arriving in Leh, which sits at around 11,500 feet above sea level. Local tourism authorities recommend at least 48 hours of rest before heading to higher-altitude areas.

If you’re determined to spot the region’s elusive snow leopard too, a good local guide is essential, and they book up fast. Hemis National Park is one of the world's best-known places to search for these big cats, with experienced trackers scanning the rocky slopes and valleys for signs of movement. Unlike conventional trekking holidays, snow leopard expeditions are best undertaken during the colder months, generally between November and April, when specialist wildlife tours operate in the region. The conditions can be challenging, with freezing temperatures and unpredictable mountain weather, but the rewards can be extraordinary. Ladakh is at its loveliest, and busiest, during the warmer months, from June to September, for those interested in exploring its Buddhist monasteries.

Consider booking through Voygr Expeditions, andBeyond, or Responsible Travel, all of which offer specialist snow leopard expeditions with experienced local guides or trackers. Some itineraries also incorporate visits to local communities and conservation initiatives, including andBeyond's support for the Snow Leopard Conservancy. With several 2027 departures already sold out, securing a place six to 12 months ahead is advisable, especially for those hoping to travel during the peak winter months.

For decades, safari trips centered around Big Five game, but Rwanda has something that Kenya, Zambia, and Botswana do not: silverback mountain gorillas. As a country, Rwanda has been a champion of ecotourism since long before the term went mainstream, with reforestation, conservation, and caps on visitor numbers protecting the environment and the wildlife within it. These efforts have contributed to a remarkable conservation success story, with the mountain gorilla population across the Virunga Massif, which spans Rwanda, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing from 480 in 2010 to 604 in 2016. In the Virunga Mountains, only eight people may trek to visit a particular gorilla group each day, with encounters limited to one hour. Visitors are told to stay at least 23 feet away to protect the gorillas from human diseases, although the animals themselves may occasionally approach more closely (recall David Attenborough’s encounter in 1978, when he commented, ‘There is more meaning and mutual understanding in exchanging a glance with a gorilla than any other animal I know’).

A collection of established luxury lodges, such as Magashi Camp, Singita Kwitonda Lodge, One&Only’s Gorilla’s Nest, and Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort have proven themselves to experienced safari-goers. While Magashi offers traditional Big Five game drives in Akagera National Park, Singita Kwitonda and Gorilla's Nest provide luxurious bases for gorilla trekking, and Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort is ideally placed for exploring the rainforest and tracking chimpanzees. For those wanting to venture beyond the forests, Lake Kivu offers a completely different perspective on Rwanda's landscapes. The Kivu Queen uBuranga, which began welcoming guests in December 2023, takes travelers across the lake aboard a luxury floating hotel, with opportunities to explore its islands and discover local communities and traditions.

Gorilla trekking permits currently cost $1,500 per person for most international visitors, and with only eight visitors allowed per habituated gorilla group each day, booking several months in advance is strongly recommended, particularly during the drier seasons from June to September and December to February. Those hoping to combine gorilla trekking with a stay at one of the country's most exclusive lodges should start planning even earlier, especially if traveling during peak holiday periods.

A version of this story originally appeared in Condé Nast Traveller UK.

As the most discerning, up-to-the-minute voice in all things travel, Condé Nast Traveler is the global citizen’s bible and muse, offering both inspiration and vital intel. We understand that time is the greatest luxury, which is why Condé Nast Traveler mines its network of experts and influencers so that you never waste a meal, a drink, or a hotel stay wherever you are in the world.

Is airline elite status worth it anymore? It’s an age-old question that’s back on plenty of travelers’ minds — especially after two of the four largest U.S. carriers overhauled their loyalty programs this month.

And one theme is becoming clear: To get the best rewards, members are going to have to spend ... a lot.

Starting in 2027, taking the most United Airlines flights won’t necessarily translate to the highest United MileagePlus status.

Instead, the airline's top elite members will be the customers who spend the most money — either on flights or the airline’s cobranded credit cards.

Top-tier 1K status will also be harder to earn.

Meanwhile, Southwest Airlines took its biggest step yet toward nudging flyers toward its lineup of credit cards.

Beginning next year, every dollar its members charge to their Southwest Rapid Rewards cards will count toward status.

Southwest also closed a key shortcut to its most alluring perk: the Companion Pass. Going forward, members hoping to score the "buy-one, get-one" flight pass will have to spend their way to the airline’s top status tier (or take 100 flights in a year).

These changes weren’t entirely surprising.

Over the past decade, airline status has become less about the time you spend in the sky and more about the cash you’re willing to spend.

For years, American Airlines and Delta Air Lines have awarded status based purely on the money their frequent flyers spend.

And across the industry, carriers have become more agnostic about whether those dollars come in the form of a flight booking or card swipe at the grocery store.

On some airlines, you can now technically swipe your way to status without ever setting foot on a plane.

Here’s how much you’d need to pay for top-tier airline status in 2027 — if you went exclusively by credit card spending.

*Note: American has not announced what its status thresholds will be in 2027.

Note: United requires a minimum of four United-operated flights for members to be Premier-eligible.

Note: Cardholders earn a one-time 10,000 TQP boost upon hitting 130,000 TQPs in 2027.

Note: Elite credit earned by flying or other eligible spending reduces the card spending needed to qualify for elite status. Southwest still also offers elite qualification via flight segments.

It’s not just the eye-popping dollar amounts travelers must now spend to reach status.

Airlines have also made carrying a credit card a more important part of the overall loyalty experience.

United and Delta cardholders now get access to better mileage redemptions than members who don’t carry a card.

JetBlue will soon offer exclusive elite perks to JetBlue TrueBlue loyalty members who carry its top-tier card.

And even more airlines offer cardholders shortcuts to elite status.

Delta this month said it’s on track to pull in a record $9 billion through its banking partnership with American Express.

American expects to make $8 billion this year through its tie-up with Citibank.

Those are eye-popping numbers, of course.

Beyond the raw cash flow, though, airlines also see turning flyers into cardholders as one of the best ways to become part of customers’ day-to-day lives, even when they’re not on a trip.

“It really is about making sure that we are top of mind for our members every single day, whether or not they’re able to be on board our aircraft," Jarad Fisher, United’s president of MileagePlus, said in a recent interview.

On one hand, airline status still offers a host of ways to save money, get better seats and travel with more flexible policies.

And, in some ways, qualify has become more realistic for travelers who aren’t true “road warriors," since everyday spending counts toward status.

At the same time, free first-class upgrades have gotten harder to score and status benchmarks keep getting pricier to earn.

It's created a real dilemma for travelers who fly a lot — but only have so much money they're willing to put toward earning status: Is it worth dumping tens (or hundreds) of thousands of dollars onto your favorite airline’s credit card to reach your status goal?

Think about what you’re getting out of status, and whether it’s worth the investment.

If not, you could be a candidate to hop off the status "hamster wheel" and be an airline "free agent."

But if you've crunched the numbers and decided status is still worth it, you may need to double down on your favorite airline.

And that might mean prioritizing credit card spending on that carrier's card. Because in 2026, that is almost as important as flying when it comes to unlocking the best perks.

Here’s how much you’d need to pay for entry-tier airline status in 2027 if you went exclusively by credit card spending.

*Note: American has not announced what its status thresholds will be in 2027.

$25,000 with the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® (see rates and fees)

Assumes 12 flight segments on American to fully unlock the card’s “Flight Streak” benefit.

$25,000 with the Delta SkyMiles® Reserve American Express Card

Note: United requires a minimum of four United-operated flights for members to be Premier-eligible.

$35,000 with any cobranded credit card, including the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card

Of course, the most efficient way to earn status is by combining your card spending with flying.

Spending on flights does typically earn you more elite credit (and points) than you'd get with typical credit card spending.

While airline credit cards can offer strong value with that carrier, other cards may offer a stronger return for your spending.

For instance, there's basically no airline card that truly competes with the American Express® Gold Card on rewards for dining worldwide and grocery purchases.

And some Capital One credit cards offer 2 miles per dollar spent on every purchase.

Most of us only have so many dollars to dole out, and sometimes the best rewards to earn are the flexible points you can transfer to a wide range of partners.

Plus, as a frequent traveler, I also carry hotel cards that are key to unlocking perks once I arrive at my destination.

If you're rethinking your loyalty with a particular airline, there are status matches you can take advantage of to effectively “change airlines.”

Just remember: Most U.S. carriers are now playing the “spending to status” game in some form. So, you may encounter similar sticker shock with your new carrier of choice.

Plus, even after matching, you’ll likely have to hit an ambitious challenge goal to keep your status for the entire year.

While United and Southwest announced major overhauls to their loyalty and status programs, Delta opted to stay the course for next year.

Its Medallion qualification requirements will not change in 2027.

Delta’s last major shake-up to its Delta SkyMiles program came in 2023, which led to significant backlash among its SkyMiles members.

American likely won’t update its AAdvantage members for a few months since its loyalty year technically doesn’t begin until March 1.

So, it remains to be seen whether the status game will continue getting harder for more flyers in the new year.

#6234. American Airlines Expected To Nearly Double Size Of Philadelphia Flagship Lounge

Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America. Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand. His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

The world's largest airline by passenger volume, American Airlines is eyeing a Flagship Lounge expansion at Philadelphia International Airport (PHL). American is considering absorbing the airport's Philadelphia A West Admirals Club into its Flagship as soon as March next year.

These plans, which have been analyzed by View From The Wing and Inside Flyer, came to light when a lounge staff member made comments to a visiting passenger. However, the airline has since confirmed publicly that no lounge plans are final and that the proposed expansion plan could double the total Flagship space.

With these plans having the potential to be completed by the Spring, this would prepare the airline ahead of the summer peak. The current Flagship lounge covers a total of 12,500 square feet (1,161 square meters) and has the capacity to seat 200 guests. Its neighboring Admirals A West Club covers a total of 11,000 square feet (1,021 square meters) and has the capacity for up to 181 guests.

The two lounges are already connected, but with the plans for a full takeover by Flagship of the Admirals Club, the two lounges would merge into a large 25,000 square feet (2,322 square meters) complex.

Simple Flying reached out to the airline for comment and further details on the plan; however, an airline spokesperson could not immediately be reached.

For the oneworld carrier, the consideration to merge both the Flagship and Admirals Club lounges would address the steady increase in overcrowding that is seen during the airport's transatlantic departure bank. During the summer, American boosts its European schedule, adding hundreds of flights across the Northern Hemisphere summer season.

This results in thousands more weekly passengers through the airport terminals, and frequent flyers or those eligible for lounge access are putting a strain on the current setup. American is now considering the takeover of the Admirals Club to address this demand before the next seasonal rush. Below is the full list of year-round and seasonal transatlantic services offered by American from Philadelphia:

Amsterdam (AMS), Dublin (DUB), Lisbon (LIS), London–Heathrow (LHR), Madrid (MAD), Paris–Charles de Gaulle (CDG), Rome–Fiumicino (FCO), Zurich (ZRH)

Athens (ATH), Budapest (BUD), Copenhagen (CPH), Edinburgh (EDI), Milan–Malpensa (MXP), Naples (NAP), Nice (NCE), Prague (PRG), Venice (VCE)

Next summer, additional new seasonal services will be added to Porto (OPO) from March 28, Vienna International Airport (VIE) from May 6, and Reykjavik (KEF) on May 27.

Philadelphia is an important base for American, with more than 300 flights recorded daily. It remains the busiest airport in the state of Pennsylvania, and one of the busiest airports in the United States. It is a major airport for the airline's European network.

American Airlines is doubling down on Philadelphia, where 21 nonstop European routes underscore its role as the carrier’s transatlantic powerhouse.

With the airline still to confirm whether the lounge takeover will proceed, the move would provide additional Flagship seating for its premium travelers. As a result, this would leave those members who currently access the Admirals A West lounge forced to take a longer walk to the Admirals Club available in B and C.

Philadelphia Terminal A is the primary international terminal, with both the American Airlines Flagship and Admirals Club. Other lounges include British Airways Galleries Lounge and American Express Centurion Lounge. Nearby, Terminals B and C are used for the majority of domestic and other short-haul international flights.

The current Terminal A Admirals Club is open from 5:00 AM through to 10:00 PM daily, and provides complimentary food and drinks, a full-service bar, free Wi-Fi, and showers. There are no conference rooms available. Next door, at the Flagship Lounge, this facility remains open from 8:00 AM to 9:30 PM. Both of these lounges are located on the mezzanine level between Gates A15 and A16.

The Flagship lounge is available for qualifying First and Business class travelers, eligible AAdvantage and Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards members, those with ConciergeKey, alongside other oneworld Emerald or Sapphire status tier holders.

#6231. Denver Air Connection Plans First Florida Service

Denver Air Connection will launch its first-ever service to Florida, and it will be outside the scope of any Essential Air Service (EAS) contract. The only other place in the carrier’s network that isn’t directly part of an EAS contract is its service to Telluride, Colorado, from both Denver and Phoenix.

Beginning January 9, 2027, DAC will begin nonstop flights from Muskegon, Michigan, to Orlando Sanford, with service operating on Saturdays using the 50-seat Embraer E145XR.

While Muskegon itself only has one other destination, Chicago O’Hare, which is also operated by DAC under the EAS contract, DAC will compete indirectly with Allegiant, as it has a sizable operation and a base in Grand Rapids, Michigan, which is located only about 45 minutes east of Muskegon.

The 1,030-mile route from Muskegon to Orlando Sanford on the E145 will become the longest at-risk flight operated by any EAS carrier, and one of the longest commercial airline flights operated by an Embraer E145 in the country, overtaking the current record holder, United’s 830-mile route from Washington Dulles to Mobile, Alabama, by almost 200 miles.

That record for the E145 is a little bit of a technicality, as JSX does operate a handful of flights over 1,000 miles with its Embraer E145s, but the carrier is not considered a commercial airline, and is instead classified as a “public charter operation.”

Muskegon Airport director Ken Efting did have something to say about this new service: “This is a historic milestone for MKG and the communities we serve…This is exactly the kind of opportunity we’ve been working toward, and it’s a testament to our growing community support and strong partnership with Denver Air Connection.”

This isn’t the first time an EAS carrier has operated at-risk service to the state of Florida from an EAS community. These smaller carriers sometimes begin flights to leisure destinations like Florida and other leisure-heavy destinations to entice higher passenger numbers that boost the communities they serve.

Muskegon will join the small but growing list of Essential Air Service communities that are now connected with nonstop flights to the state of Florida, but they will be the only EAS community in Michigan to have Florida flights.

#6230. Not Port-au-Prince: American Airlines Returns To Haiti After 2+ Years With All-Haitian Crew

American Airlines has resumed flights to Haiti, launching daily nonstop service between Miami International Airport (MIA) and Cap-Haïtien International Airport (CAP) on November 1. The return makes American the first major US network carrier to restore service to the country since US airlines suspended flights amid escalating security concerns in 2024. Its inaugural flight carried an all-Haitian, Creole-speaking crew led by Captain Oliver Jean, giving the restart additional significance for the Haitian diaspora and communities on both sides of the route.

However, the service does not extend to Port-au-Prince. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) continues to restrict US commercial operators from flying into the Haitian capital because of security threats, including armed attacks on aircraft. Instead, American has selected Cap-Haïtien in northern Haiti, restoring a connection through its Miami hub while avoiding the airport at the center of the country's aviation security crisis.

Daily flights between Miami and Cap-Haïtien provide travelers with a direct connection to northern Haiti, where American previously operated service between 2014 and 2020. Although the airline has served Haiti since 1971, it had not flown to Cap-Haïtien for more than six years before the latest launch.

American is operating the route with Boeing 737 aircraft, providing more than 90 onward connections across the United States through Miami. That network access is particularly relevant for Haitian-American communities outside South Florida, including travelers in New York and Orlando, who can connect through the airline’s hub rather than relying on less convenient itineraries. The entirely Haitian crew highlighted the personal and cultural connections between the airline and the communities served by the route. For passengers traveling to visit relatives, conduct business, or return home, having a direct flight operated by a major US carrier restores an option that had been missing since the industry-wide suspension.

American described Cap-Haïtien as its 100th destination in the Caribbean and Latin America network. The milestone adds to a regional footprint that the airline says is larger than that of any other US carrier, while giving northern Haiti a direct link to one of the country's most important international gateways.

"The continued growth of our network in the region — including being the first airline to return to Venezuela earlier this year — is a reflection of the legacy we’ve built and one we’re proud to carry forward as we continue growing our network across the region.”

- Vice President of International Operations José A. Freig

Security concerns explain why American can serve Cap-Haïtien but not the capital. In November 2024, gunfire struck aircraft operated by American, JetBlue, and Spirit Airlines near Port-au-Prince. The incidents prompted US carriers to suspend service, while the FAA introduced restrictions on civil aviation operations in affected parts of Haiti. The agency subsequently narrowed its restrictions, allowing US aircraft to operate at airports outside the designated area around the capital. Cap-Haïtien, located in northern Haiti, falls beyond the restricted airspace. Port-au-Prince’s Toussaint Louverture International Airport (PAP) still remains inaccessible to commercial carriers from the US under the current rules.

Geographic separation has allowed international service to continue at Cap-Haïtien, and the northern airport is therefore an important entry point for travelers heading to Haiti, although reaching destinations in the south may require additional ground transportation and careful consideration of local security conditions. American’s return does not signify that conditions have normalized across the country.

With multiple domestic and international routes coming, most of the carrier's hubs are involved. Find out more here!

Miami's importance to the new route extends beyond its proximity to Haiti. American operates more than 410 peak daily flights from the airport to over 170 destinations in 46 countries, making it the carrier's most internationally connected hub. The additional Haiti service gives passengers access to that network, including connections from cities that do not have nonstop flights to Cap-Haïtien. South Florida is home to the largest Haitian-American population in the United States, making the Miami connection especially significant for family visits and other regular travel.

For now, American's daily Miami-Cap-Haïtien flights represent a meaningful reopening of one part of the US-Haiti air market. The all-Haitian inaugural crew gave the launch a distinctive community connection, but the larger development is the restoration of a major airline link. Whether service can eventually extend to Port-au-Prince will depend on security improvements and the FAA's willingness to lift its remaining restrictions.

#6228. Southwest Premier Card Review: Is The $149 Mid-Range Card Worth It?

Chase and Southwest have a great portfolio of personal credit cards at three different price points. This is my in-depth review of the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Premier Credit Card, the Southwest personal card with a $149 annual fee (which is neither the highest nor lowest annual fee product).

Now is an especially good time to consider this card, both because it’s offering an elevated welcome bonus, and because it’s your last chance to use credit card welcome bonuses to qualify for Southwest’s Companion Pass benefit under the old system.

Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Premier Credit Card

Before I get into my Southwest Premier Card review, here’s a broad look at the card and its key features:

In my opinion, here are the pros and cons of the Southwest Airlines Premier Card:

When applying for credit, cards, the welcome bonus, eligibility rules, and fees, are obviously major factors that potential cardmembers consider. So let’s cover those details for the Southwest Premier Card, as the card has a great bonus, nuanced eligibility requirements, and a relatively manageable annual fee.

The Southwest Premier Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you can earn 85,000 bonus points after you spend $2,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. This is a limited time, elevated offer, as the most recent base offer was for 55,000 points.

Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program. Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Rapid Rewards points to be worth 1.2 cents each. So to me, the points from this welcome bonus are worth $1,020, making this a solid welcome offer.

When it comes to Southwest credit card eligibility rules, the Southwest Premier Card isn’t available to anyone who currently has a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card, or anyone who has received a welcome bonus on a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card in the past 24 months. However, you are eligible if you have a Southwest Rapid Rewards business credit card.

Beyond the restrictions related to which Southwest cards you have, there are general application rules for Chase cards, including the Chase 5/24 rule, whereby you usually won’t get approved for a Chase credit card if you’ve opened five or more credit card accounts in the past 24 months.

The Southwest Premier Card has a $149 annual fee, and you can add authorized users to the card at no extra cost. Southwest’s personal credit cards have annual fees of $99, $149, and $229, so this is the “middle child” of the Southwest and Chase personal card portfolio.

The Southwest Premier Card has no foreign transaction fees, so you can use it abroad without worrying about extra charges.

In addition to the benefits, one of the main reasons you’ll want to consider picking up a card is because of its return on spending, so you’re sure it aligns with what you’re looking for. In the case of the Southwest Premier Card, it has a limited number of bonus categories, and spending can also help you toward earning elite status with Rapid Rewards. So let’s cover those details.

As far as the Southwest Premier Card’s rewards structure goes, the card offers the following:

It’s good that the card has some bonus categories, though there are ultimately more rewarding cards out there for everyday spending. Based on my valuation of 1.2 cents per point, that’s like a 3.6% return on Southwest purchases, a 2.4% return on grocery stores and restaurants (up to the cap), and a 1.2% return on everything else.

The Southwest Premier Card also lets you earn unlimited Tier Qualifying Points (TQPs) toward Southwest status. Through the end of 2026, you can earn 1,500 TQPs toward A-List status for every $5,000 spent on the card. Starting January 1, 2027, every Southwest credit card will earn 1 TQP per dollar spent, so $35,000 in spending on any of them would get you to Silver status.

A-List is Southwest Airlines’ version of elite status, and offers perks like priority boarding, a 25% points bonus, same-day standby, priority check-in and security lane access, and a dedicated phone number. A-List status ordinarily requires earning 35,000 TQPs in a calendar year, so spending on a Southwest Premier Card could help you earn that. Whether or not that’s worth it depends on how much you’d otherwise fly with Southwest.

Currently, Southwest Rapid Rewards elite status has two levels: A-List and A-List Preferred. Beginning January 1, 2027, though, the program will grow to three tiers, with new names: Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Qualifying for Silver status will require the same 35,000 TQPs needed for A-List, while Gold and Platinum will require 65,000 TQPs and 140,000 TQPs, respectively. I covered these Southwest Rapid Rewards program changes in detail here.

This brings me to another big upcoming change to the Southwest program and how cards like the Southwest Premier Card fit into your strategy — and this is a pretty unwelcome one.

One of the best values in travel is the Southwest Airlines Companion Pass. With a Companion Pass, you can have someone travel with you for the entire year (whether on a cash ticket or award ticket) and just pay taxes and fees for them. This is such an incredible deal and basically doubles the value you can get from flying Southwest.

For a long time now, the points earned as part of Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have counted towards the 135,000 qualifying points needed to earn the Companion Pass. But starting January 1, 2027, credit card welcome bonuses will no longer count toward qualification.

This eliminates the easiest way to earn this valuable benefit, and it’s not the only change: referral bonuses, anniversary points, bonus points from spending, and partner spending, won’t count toward the Companion Pass either. In fact, Southwest’s rolling the Companion Pass into its highest elite tier, Platinum, and requiring either 140,000 TQPs or 100 qualifying flights to earn it.

This change isn’t specific to the Southwest Premier Card, as it applies to welcome bonuses across all Southwest credit cards. But the good news is that welcome bonuses earned before the end of 2026 do count toward Companion Pass qualification, so now is your last chance to take advantage before this opportunity ends.

I have a dedicated post that covers how to redeem Southwest Rapid Rewards points for maximum value, but I’ll briefly cover how redemptions work.

Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, which means that the value you’ll get from your points is tied to the cash cost of Southwest tickets. That said, there are a few different levels, ranging from Basic tickets to Choice Extra fares.

Basic award fares tend to offer the highest redemption value, and in my experience the best-value Southwest point redemptions are usually for international routes to destinations like Costa Rica and Aruba. For instance, I’ve seen Basic awards from Tampa (TPA) to Liberia, Costa Rica (LIR) for 12,000 points and $24.21. The same fare cost $200 in cash, giving you a very strong value of 1.46 cents per point.

One great thing about the Southwest Rapid Rewards program is that there are no change or cancellation fees, and rebooking a fare when the price drops gets you a refund equal to any difference in points. Just note that Basic fares can only be changed by upgrading to a higher fare bundle, so for a cheaper Basic award you’d cancel and rebook rather than change.

The Southwest Airlines Premier Card offers some benefits that could make the card worth keeping long term. How do the perks compare to Southwest’s lower and higher annual fee cards?

The Southwest Premier Card gets the primary cardholder and up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation a first checked bag at no additional cost. Checked bags on Southwest cost $45 each way, so this can save you up to $90 roundtrip on checked bag fees per person. With even a couple of roundtrip flights per year, this benefit can offset the annual fee.

The Southwest Airlines Premier Card lets you pick a Preferred seat on Southwest, if any are available, starting 48 hours before departure. The cost for a Preferred seat can vary from $28 to nearly $50 depending on the flight, so this perk is another potential money-saver.

Another Southwest Premier Card benefit is early boarding. You’ll be able to board with Group 5, or earlier if you have elite status or a fare or seat type that qualifies you for an earlier boarding group. Southwest has eight total boarding groups, so while there are several ahead of Group 5, it’s better than boarding last.

On your cardmember anniversary every year, you’ll receive 6,000 bonus Rapid Rewards points. Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and you can generally expect that you’ll need around 83 Rapid Rewards points for every dollar of airfare you book.

In other words, 6,000 bonus points get you around $72 in Southwest airfare annually. That covers nearly half of the annual fee right there.

Each year on your Southwest Premier Card cardmember anniversary, you’ll get a 15% promo code that applies to Southwest flights. Just note that this excludes Basic fares.

The Southwest Premier Card offers 25% savings on inflight purchases of Wi-Fi and drinks. Simply pay with your card, and you’ll automatically receive a statement credit for that amount.

The Southwest Premier Card offers a variety of travel & purchase protection benefits, including:

You’ll want to check the cardmember agreement for the full terms & conditions associated with these benefits.

The Southwest Airlines Premier Card is Southwest’s mid-range card, and the $149 annual fee is in line with many other co-branded airline credit cards. The card is offering a fantastic bonus, which is one good reason to consider this product.

On an ongoing basis, the 6,000-point anniversary bonus can get you around $72 worth of airfare. Whether the Southwest Premier Card is worth it in the long run depends on how much you value the other perks like a free checked bag, and whether you plan to use spending on the credit card to qualify for Southwest elite status.

As I mentioned above, the Southwest Premier Card is the mid-range option in Chase’s lineup of Southwest cards. Here’s a look at how it compares to the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card (learn more), which is the entry-level option:

If you don’t care about working toward Southwest status through credit card spending and you want to keep your annual fee to a minimum, the Southwest Plus Card is likely a better option for you.

On the other end of the spectrum, there’s the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card, which is the most expensive of the three personal Southwest credit cards. Here’s how it differs from the Southwest Premier Card:

If you fly Southwest all the time and want as many benefits with the airline as possible, the Southwest Priority Card could be the right choice. It’s also the best pick if you want to spend your way toward status before the end of 2026, since it earns TQPs at the fastest rate of the three cards.

Chase Ultimate Rewards is a transfer partner with Southwest Rapid Rewards, and points transfer at a 1:1 ratio. This means that you could earn points at a faster rate through Ultimate Rewards than through Rapid Rewards, and your points will be more flexible (since you can also transfer them to other airlines and hotel programs).

So, should you earn Rapid Rewards points directly with a Southwest Airlines credit card, or with a Chase Ultimate Rewards credit card?

For context, some of the best cards for earning Chase Ultimate Rewards points include the following:

On top of that, the following four no annual fee cards earn points that can be converted into Ultimate Rewards points at a 1:1 ratio in conjunction with one of the above cards:

The Southwest Premier Card is a solid mid-range airline credit card. It has a nice welcome bonus, plus ongoing perks that justify the annual fee. However, if you’re not particularly interested in extra perks when you fly Southwest, you’re much better off earning points with Chase Ultimate Rewards and then transferring them to Southwest Rapid Rewards, given that it gives you higher points earning rates and more flexibility.

If you want to learn more about the Southwest Premier Card, follow this link.

Earn 2 Delta Comfort Flight Certificates + 50K Miles

The Business Platinum Card® from American Express

As High As 300,000 points. Find Out Your Offer.

Earn up to $4,300 in travel value when you spend $120,000 in your first 4 months as a cardholder

Earn up to $4,300 in travel value when you spend $120,000 in your first 4 months as a cardholder

Here's the fun part about American Express Membership Rewards: You don't necessarily need to spend more to earn more points. You need the right card in your hand at the right time.

The best Amex setup shouldn't require a flowchart. It should feel almost effortless, with your points balance growing in the background while every card earns its keep.

These are the four Amex cards I'd choose to maximize your Membership Rewards balance, whether you're looking for one great earner or a multifaceted points strategy.

These cards made my list because each has a distinct job. Most people won't need all four, but picking the right one (or complementary pair) can help your existing spending earn 2, 4 or even 5 points per dollar instead of just 1 point per dollar.

Want a single card to handle your personal expenses? For that, the American Express Gold Card is the workhorse of an Amex points strategy.

It earns 4 points per dollar at U.S. supermarkets on up to $25,000 in purchases each calendar year and at restaurants worldwide on up to $50,000, then 1 point per dollar. If groceries and dining are a large share of your budget, these bonus categories can build your points balance quickly.

The Gold isn't limited to food, either. It earns:

That range makes it my strongest one-card recommendation for someone who wants to earn Membership Rewards points across both everyday spending and travel.

The card has a $325 annual fee (see ), but includes up to $10 monthly Uber Cash for eligible U.S. Uber and Uber Eats orders†, up to $10 monthly dining statement credit with select partners and up to $50 biannual statement credits at U.S. Resy restaurants. (Enrollment is required for select benefits.)

That makes the fee easiest to justify for someone who will use the statement credits naturally and put the earning categories to work. Still, the credits are supporting actors here: The strong bonus categories are why the Gold deserves top billing.

If, like me, you spend about $800 per month at the grocery store, that alone will earn you 38,400 points annually. If you also spend $500 per month on dining, $3,000 per year in flights and $1,000 in prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel, your annual haul climbs to 76,400 points.

That's worth over $1,500 according to TPG’s October 2026 valuations.

Personally, I'd be tempted to transfer 60,000 of those points to Air France-KLM Flying Blue for a one-way business-class saver award between the U.S. and Europe. Those seats can be difficult to find, but that's the kind of redemption that makes my grocery runs feel more rewarding.

†Uber Cash will only be deposited into one Uber account when you add the Amex Gold as a payment method and redeem with any Amex card.

To learn more, read our full review of the American Express Gold Card.

Airfare is where the American Express Platinum Card gets its chance to flex.

The card earns 5 points per dollar on flights purchased directly from airlines or through American Express Travel®, including through AmexTravel.com and the Amex Travel App, on up to $500,000 in these purchases each calendar year (then 1 point per dollar). It also earns 5 points per dollar on prepaid lodging booked through Amex Travel and 1 point per dollar on all other eligible purchases.

Spending $4,000 on airfare each year would earn 20,000 Membership Rewards points on the Platinum card. That's worth about $400 according to our valuations, compared to just $40 earned on a 1% cash-back credit card. That level of spending isn’t outlandish: A family of four paying $500 per ticket for two trips a year would reach it. I usually travel more than twice a year, so that difference can add up even faster.

Don't overlook the fact that these rewards come from booking flights directly with the airline, either. Buying straight from the source instead of through a travel portal can make it easier to change or cancel your reservation if your plans change, or when you have to make last-minute adjustments due to delays or operational cancellations.

The Platinum carries an $895 annual fee (see ), so it makes the most sense for frequent flyers who can pair the airfare earnings with benefits they'll also use. My favorites are its broad airport lounge access through the American Express Global Lounge Collection, up to $200 in annual airline fee statement credits for incidental charges with one selected qualifying airline and complimentary Hilton Honors Gold status. Enrollment is required for select benefits.

To learn more, read our full review of the American Express Platinum Card.

Every business has expenses that refuse to cooperate with bonus categories. The Blue Business Plus Credit Card from American Express makes sure those purchases still pull their weight.

The card earns 2 points per dollar spent on the first $50,000 in eligible purchases each calendar year, then 1 point per dollar. It also earns 2 points per dollar spent on prepaid hotels and other eligible travel purchases booked through amextravel.com (and those purchases don’t count toward the $50,000 annual threshold). There's also no annual fee (see ).

That makes the Blue Business Plus an excellent catch-all card for eligible business owners. Rather than worrying about whether each purchase falls into the right merchant category, you can use it for general business spending and know you’re earning twice the standard rate until you hit the annual cap.

Maxing out the threshold with $50,000 in business expenses would earn 100,000 Membership Rewards points. If your business values simplicity more than squeezing every last penny out of a redemption, one of the easiest options is to use those points to cover $1,000 in airfare booked through Amex Travel. Transferring your points to travel partners might be worth even more.

It isn’t the flashiest card in the Amex portfolio, but quietly doubling your points on broad business spending is a skill worth having.

To learn more, read our full review of the Blue Business Plus Credit Card.

Related: Who qualifies for a business credit card?

Some businesses spend a little everywhere. Others have two or three expense categories that swallow the budget whole.

The American Express Business Gold Card is built for the latter. It automatically earns 4 points per dollar in the two eligible categories where your business spends the most each billing cycle, on up to $150,000 in combined purchases each calendar year, then 1 point per dollar.

My favorite part: Amex automatically identifies your two highest eligible spending categories each billing cycle, so you don't need a crystal ball to make a selection in advance, and you don't have to analyze your expenses line by line to choose a category after the fact. The strongest categories can even change from month to month, allowing the card to adapt to your business rather than forcing your business to follow the card.

A business putting $50,000 of qualifying expenses on the card would earn 200,000 Membership Rewards points, even without maxing out the full annual bonus threshold. One way I’d put those points to work is by transferring them to Aeroplan. That balance would cover two round-trip tickets from Miami to Rio de Janeiro — in business class.

The card has a $375 annual fee (see ), so its sweet spot is a business with enough qualifying spending to put the 4-point-per-dollar rate to serious use. For smaller or more varied expenses, the Blue Business Plus may be the easier fit.

To learn more, read our full review of the American Express Business Gold Card.

For most customers, holding all four cards is overkill, but pairing two together can supercharge your earnings compared to carrying a single card.

For personal spending, the Gold does most of the earning work on its own with its generous earning rates. Adding the Platinum improves your rewards on flights, but the combination is better evaluated as using the Gold as your primary earner and the Platinum as a way to enhance your experience through its many benefits and statement credits.

The business pairing is much easier to defend. Use the Business Gold for purchases in your two highest eligible bonus categories and the Blue Business Plus for everything else. One handles the obvious expenses; the other cleans up everything left behind.

If you're juggling both personal and business expenses, my pick is for the personal Gold and Blue Business Plus. Between the two, you'll earn 2 to 4 points per dollar on an impressive number of charges while paying only one annual fee.

Welcome offers are exciting, but short-lived. Long-term point maximization comes from paying with the right card.

And the best Amex card for earning Membership Rewards points depends on where you spend the most.

I may dream of an infinite points balance, but the goal isn't to collect every shiny Amex card; it’s to make more of my spending earn 2, 4 or 5 points per dollar.

For personal spending, the Gold is a strong choice for groceries and dining, while the Platinum can provide additional value for frequent flyers who use its premium travel benefits. Business owners may prefer the Blue Business Plus for everyday purchases or the Business Gold for concentrated spending in its bonus categories.

Once your biggest expenses earn more than 1 point per dollar, all that's left is remembering which card to use when it's time to pay and letting the points pile up from spending you were already doing.

#6226. Which Credit Card Should You Use For Marriott Hotel Stays? Here’s The Math

When you’re staying at a Marriott property, what’s the best credit card to use to maximize your return on Marriott hotel spending? Should you use a co-branded Marriott credit card, or are you better off using another credit card offering bonus points on travel? This is a question that comes up every so often, so I’d like to address it in this post…

I’ve written in the past about the best credit cards to use for hotel stays. However, more specifically to Marriott, which credit card should you put all of your Marriott spending on? Let’s take a look at the various approaches that you can take.

Let me start by acknowledging that we all value points currencies differently, so you should apply your own valuation to the math. My below analysis is based on my own valuation of various points currencies.

I also want to emphasize that the credit card you use won’t impact your ability to earn elite qualifying nights, take advantage of elite perks, and accrue the standard points that you can earn with the Marriott Bonvoy program. The credit card rewards offered when paying for your Marriott hotel stay are incremental.

Marriott has co-branded credit cards in the United States that are issued by both American Express and Chase. All of these credit cards with annual fees have the same rewards structure for Marriott spending, as they offer 6x Marriott Bonvoy® Points on all eligible Marriott spending.

This includes cards like the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card (learn more), Marriott Bonvoy Business® American Express® Card (learn more), and Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card (learn more), just to name a few. Personally, I value Bonvoy points at 0.7 cents each, so to me these cards offer an incremental 4.2% return on that spending.

I think the one thing worth pointing out is that the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card offers 1,000 Bonvoy bonus points per Marriott stay when paying with the card, in addition to the rewards that you usually earn.

Technically that would be the best co-branded card for Marriott spending, since you earn 6x points, plus 1,000 bonus points per stay. That being said, I’d otherwise consider this to be one of the less compelling Marriott cards in terms of the overall value proposition.

I generally recommend putting most of your spending on cards earning transferable points currencies, given that they offer the most flexible rewards, and also have excellent bonus categories.

I’d argue that the two best cards for hotel spending are the Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card (learn more) and Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (learn more), as they offer 4x transferable points for direct hotel purchases. Since I value Ultimate Rewards points at 1.7 cents each, that’s like a 6.8% return on that spending, which is excellent.

It’s worth noting that there are other cards earning 3x points on hotels, like the Citi Strata Premier® Card (learn more), and I’d value that at a return of 5.1%. Lastly, the Wells Fargo Autograph Journey Card (learn more) actually offers 5x points on hotel purchases, which is excellent, though I don’t value those points as much as other transferable points currencies.

Personally, the Chase Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve Business are my go-to cards for hotel spending. Simply put, I can’t turn down 4x Ultimate Rewards points, in comparison to earning 6x Bonvoy points with the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant Amex for my Marriott spending.

The difference in math is just too great, since I value 4x Ultimate Rewards points at way more than 6x Bonvoy points. But this also brings me to a related topic of how points valuations sometimes don’t dictate my consumer behavior. For example, back in the day, the Chase Sapphire Reserve offered 3x Ultimate Rewards points on hotel spending.

So I valued that at offering a 5.1% return, rather than a 4.2% return on a Marriott credit card. Despite that, I’d use a co-branded Marriott card for my Marriott spending. Why? Well, this gets at a consideration that’s hard to factor into my valuation of points. I’m talking about the ease of earning various points currencies.

I can earn transferable points currencies in all kinds of ways, including with my everyday spending. However, there aren’t many ways to efficiently earn Bonvoy points, short of staying at Marriott properties. As I often talk about when sharing my points strategy, there’s merit to collecting points that are harder to earn, even if they’re not the points currency that you necessarily value the most. This was one of those cases, at least for me. However, with the Chase Sapphire Reserve nowadays earning 4x points per dollar spent on hotels, my logic on that has evolved.

Everyone has their own credit card strategy, and at times it can be tough to decide which card is the best for a particular spending category.

In the case of spending at Marriott properties, I’d argue that the Chase Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve Business are nowadays the most lucrative, given that they offer 4x Ultimate Rewards points on that spending, which I value at a 6.8% return. I’d say that beats the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant Amex, offering 6x Bonvoy points, which I value at a 4.2% return.

Which credit card do you use for Marriott hotel spending?
